small_guidance:
- The current kernel materializes a [BLOCK_M, PK_TOTAL=128] accumulator (with BLOCK_P=8, POOL_K=16) which is huge and forces small BLOCK_M; try BLOCK_P=2 or 4 (PK_TOTAL=32 or 64) with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_K=32/64 so the `tl.dot` output tile is GEMM-friendly (128x32) and register pressure drops dramatically.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N(=PK_TOTAL)=64, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=4 — the current 8-warp configs at BLOCK_M=64,N=128 are likely register-spilling on Ada; also include a BLOCK_M=256,BLOCK_P=2 variant.
- Hoist the bias load and the pooled-tile epilogue out of the K-loop (already done), but also consider keeping `running_max` updates cheap by not re-reshaping each pt — flatten to (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_P*POOL_K) and use a strided sum via `tl.sum` over a reshaped view only once at the end of each pt iteration (current code is fine, just confirm reshape is free).
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a standard split-K GEMM-then-reduce: one program per (row-tile, N-tile) computing a BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N matmul tile with BLOCK_N aligned to POOL_K (e.g. BLOCK_N=128 = 8 pool windows), apply bias+avgpool+GELU+scale in epilogue, do an in-tile max across BLOCK_N, then atomic_max into out[B]. This decouples GEMM tile shape from pool window count and lets you use canonical 128×128×32 tiles with num_warps=8.
- Alternative: persistent kernel per row-tile that streams the entire OUT_FEATURES axis with BLOCK_N=128, keeping x_tile resident across N to maximize x reuse — since IN_FEATURES=OUT_FEATURES=8192 and B=1024, x is reloaded 64× currently; a persistent-N loop loads x once and sweeps weights, cutting x bandwidth dramatically.
- Consider fp16/bf16 weight storage with fp32 accumulate (cast at init) — weight matrix is 256MB in fp32, halving it doubles effective bandwidth and fits better in L2; the 4090 has strong fp16 tensor cores so `tl.dot` throughput jumps ~2×.
